adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which, when `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` returns true (i.e., user storage accepted the update), does not remove any existing local (Keycloak DB) `recovery-codes` credential; the local provider `createCredential(...)` is skipped in that branch (CredentialHelper.java new method). That can leave duplicated/old local recovery-codes records around. However, the finding’s stronger claim that `UserCredentialManager.isValid` “falls back” to local validators when federated validation rejects (making old codes still work) is not shown or verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, a `false` result from `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` triggers a fallback to `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)` (local DB) without removing/invalidating any existing federated recovery-codes credential. Separately, `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` explicitly prefers federated credentials first (`getFederatedCredentialsStream().findFirst()`) and only falls back to local storage if none exist. Therefore, if a federated recovery-codes credential already exists and `updateCredential` returns false for any reason (e.g., provider read-only/disabled/not updating), the newly created local codes will not be used and the old federated codes will still take precedence and remain valid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:125 — Recovery codes now go through each existing user storage provider's updateCredential, so a third-party provider whose supportsCredentialType/updateCredential return true for unknown types now swallows the codes (setup reports success but no usable credential exists), and the change is not opt-in

This is a behavior/compatibility change from the previous direct `createCredential` call in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction`. If some upstream component (e.g., a user-storage provider reached via `updateCredential`) returns `true` without actually persisting a usable recovery-codes credential, Keycloak will skip the local DB creation path. However, the claim that it will "go through each existing user storage provider" and that third-party providers "swallow" codes depends on credential-manager/provider behavior not shown in the diff, so it’s a valid risk/architecture concern but not a strictly verifiable defect from the diff alone.
